name: commitment convention changed to hash the raw seed bytes
guard: The guard that fires is Step 1. Step 1 (Seed Hash Integrity) must reject the wrong commitment convention: LIQD commits SHA-256 of the seed's HEX STRING, not of its 16 decoded bytes, and all 33 commitments stop matching.

name: seed-population pin loosened to accept a short reveal set
guard: The guard that fires is Step 1. Step 1 (Seed Hash Integrity) counts revealed seeds against EXPECTED_SEEDS from src/config.ts, never against seeds.length: 33 revealed production seeds against a pin of 32 is a population disagreement.

name: Phase A epoch size restated in the capture plan (200 -> 100)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 4. Step 4 (Nonce Audit) binds each epoch's nonce window to the capture plan in src/config.ts and not to the dataset: with the plan at 100 the 200-round Phase A epochs and their nonces 100..199 are out of contract.

name: draw domain off by one
guard: The guard that fires is Step 16. Step 16 (Effective-Edge Curve) must reject a wrong draw domain: RANGE sets the edge denominator (RANGE x SCALE) and the grid enumeration, so the 1.00% floor and the pinned population sizes stop holding. Step 5 does not fire: the scored draw is src/rng.ts limboDraw, which carries its own range.

name: HMAC cursor moved off 0
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a wrong HMAC cursor: the message clientSeed:nonce:cursor changes and the recomputed results diverge from the served ones.

name: HMAC key taken as UTF-8 text instead of hex-decoded bytes
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject the wrong key encoding: keying the HMAC with the ASCII of the 32-character seed instead of its 16 bytes produces a well-formed draw stream that only comparison against settled rounds can tell apart.

name: HMAC salt field order swapped
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a re-ordered message: every ordering of the three fields is syntactically valid, so the ordering is a claim only the settled capture can settle.

name: modulo-bias rejection guard removed
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a draw taken without the rejection guard: 135 of the 5,838 production rounds had their first chunk in the rejected tail, and 134 of them change under the guardless form (on bet QVa47RZmz6DTZoHGxY2GM it gives the same result), so Step 5 finds 134 mismatches.

name: house edge doubled
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a doubled edge: RESULT_NUMERATOR is (1 - HOUSE_EDGE) x SCALE x RANGE, so the edge IS the result formula and changing it changes the recomputed results.

name: result numerator decoupled from the edge
find: export const RESULT_NUMERATOR = (1 - HOUSE_EDGE) * MULTIPLIER_SCALE * RANGE;
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a numerator that is not (1 - edge) x scale x range.

name: result formula off by one in the divisor (k instead of k+1)
replace: return Math.min(MAX_MULTIPLIER, Math.max(MIN_RESULT, Math.floor(RESULT_NUMERATOR / k) / MULTIPLIER_SCALE));
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject an off-by-one in the divisor: dividing by k shifts results by one grid step.

name: multiplier grid widened from 2 decimals to 3
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a result computed on the wrong decimal grid; the comparison is strict equality with no tolerance.

name: result floor removed
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a model without the R = 1 floor: on 66 production rounds the raw value is below 1 and the casino served 1.

name: result floor conflated with the minimum target (1.01)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a floor at 1.01: the 116 production rounds served at 1 would all be recomputed as 1.01.

name: win rule flipped from >= to strict >
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must reject a strict-greater win rule: 2 production rounds land with the served result exactly on the chosen target (1.01x and 11.57x) and the casino settled both as wins; under > both flip to losses.

name: win rule loosened by one 2-dp tick
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must reject a rule that pays one tick short of the target: 12 production rounds land exactly one 2-dp tick below their target and the casino settled all 12 as losses.

name: 2-dp target grid computed with floor instead of round
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must reject a floored target grid: for targets whose binary64 product target x 100 falls just under the integer, the hundredths value drops by one and the target is no longer on the 2-dp grid.

name: target grid capped below the ladder top (99x)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must reject a grid that excludes targets the casino accepted: the production rounds at 100x and above are then off the grid.

name: minimum target raised above the lowest target played
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must reject a minimum target above 1.01: 110 production rounds were played at 1.01x and are then off the grid.

name: draw made stateful: every 100th recomputation returns a different value
guard: The guard that fires is Step 7. Step 7 (Recomputation Determinism) must reject a recomputation that depends on how many times it has run: the two forward passes and the reverse pass disagree.

name: money arithmetic taken to hundredths with floor instead of round
guard: The guard that fires is Step 9. Step 9 (Credit Arithmetic) must reject floored hundredths: for stakes and targets whose binary64 product with 100 falls just under the integer, the exact-decimal credit identity breaks.

name: settlement rounding switched from nearest to truncation
guard: The guard that fires is Step 20. Step 20 (Settlement Determinism) must reject truncation in the 8-dp route a re-implementer would take: on wins whose binary64 product sits just under the decimal value the truncated credit is one unit short of what the casino paid.

name: bet-population pin loosened
guard: The guard that fires is Step 12. Step 12 (Dataset Integrity & Population Identity) binds the population to EXPECTED_BETS in src/config.ts and requires the capture plan to add up to it: 5,838 rounds against a pin of 5,837 is a population disagreement.

name: Phase C stake restated at 1.00
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) must reject a plan whose Phase C stake is not the stake the 238 rounds were played at (10.00 USDT).

name: Phase A stake restated at 1.00
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) must reject a plan whose Phase A stake is not the stake the 5,100 rounds were played at (0.10 USDT).

name: Phase C win floor raised above the wins captured (100 -> 115)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) counts the elevated-stake wins that went through the payout path against the floor: 114 wins against a floor of 115 fails, so the floor is load-bearing.

name: ladder top restated (100x -> 1,000,000x)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) must reject a ladder top that is not the top of PROD_TARGET_LADDER.

name: ladder rounds-per-target pin moved (100 -> 99)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) requires each of the 50 ladder targets exactly PROD_ROUNDS_PER_TARGET times in Phase A.

name: top-up rounds at 10,000x restated (50 -> 49)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) requires exactly the planned number of top-up rounds at 10,000x: 50 captured against 49 planned fails.

name: target-coverage plan drops decade 10^4
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) must reject a coverage plan that does not declare a decade the capture played, and one that stops short of the decade of the top target.

name: runner build of run 1 restated in the capture log constants
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) requires each run's header to carry the runner build the capture log records for it.

name: Phase A decade floor raised above the top-up count (50 -> 51)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 13. Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) holds every declared decade to the profile floor: decades 10^3 and 10^4 hold 50 rounds each, so a floor of 51 fails.

name: Phase D seed count pin raised (5 -> 6)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 18. Step 18 (Client-Seed Control & Phase D) counts the distinct player-set seeds against PHASE_D_SEEDS: 5 captured against a pin of 6 fails.

name: client seed dropped from the HMAC message
guard: The guard that fires is Step 18. Step 18 (Client-Seed Control & Phase D) must reject a model in which the client seed does not enter the draw: the wrong-seed and empty-seed controls then leave every draw unchanged and no round recomputes.

name: result-comparison predicate replaced by an unconditional accept
guard: The guard that fires is Step 14. Step 14 (Anti-Circularity) must detect a comparison that cannot fail: the negative control requires the predicate to REJECT a result one tick away, NaN and Infinity.

name: result comparison given a tolerance wider than the 2-dp grid
guard: The guard that fires is Step 14. Step 14 (Anti-Circularity) must detect a tolerance: the negative control perturbs the true result by one 2-dp tick, which a 0.02 band accepts.

name: upper result clamp removed
guard: The guard that fires is Step 14. Step 14 (Anti-Circularity) exercises the grid extremes directly and requires k = 0 to give the 1,000,000x cap; Step 25 also fails, because the production verifier reports 1,000,000 on draws whose raw value is higher.

name: result cap doubled (1,000,000 -> 2,000,000)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 25. Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) recomputes the production verifier probes of evidence/E02: on the draws whose raw value is above 1,000,000 the casino replied 1,000,000, which a cap of 2,000,000 does not reproduce.

name: result-cap probe count pin raised (4 -> 5 discriminating probes)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 25. Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) counts the probes whose raw value is above the cap against the pin: 4 in the pinned records against 5 fails.

name: verifier parity comparison inverted on the win flag
find: servedResultMatches(Number(v.result), Number(b.result)) && v.win === b.win && v.multiplier === b.multiplier;
replace: servedResultMatches(Number(v.result), Number(b.result)) && v.win !== b.win && v.multiplier === b.multiplier;
guard: The guard that fires is Step 25. Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) requires the verifier's win flag to equal the settled round's on every one of the 5,838 rounds.

name: verifier probe record edited (the control's result moved one cent)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 25. Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) recomputes every probe from src/ and holds the records to their pin; Step 19 also fails on the pin.

name: E03 record edited: the verifier reply on target 100000 restated as HTTP 200
guard: The guard that fires is Step 17. Step 17 (Target Bounds & Maximum Payout) reads evidence/E03 and requires it to say what the report says about it: one verifier request at target 100000, answered HTTP 400.

name: game-page record edited: the 10,000x example removed
guard: The guard that fires is Step 17. Step 17 (Target Bounds & Maximum Payout) reads the game page record and requires the sentence the report quotes as the page's top example.

name: highest settled target restated (10,000 -> 9,999)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 17. Step 17 (Target Bounds & Maximum Payout) must reject an audited range that excludes targets the capture played: 50 rounds at 10,000x are then above it. Steps 11, 13, 16 and 21 fail with it.

name: win chance rounded UP instead of floored
guard: The guard that fires is Step 15. Step 15 (Win-Chance vs Result-Distribution Identity) requires the win chance to equal the number of winning draws on the grid, as an integer identity.

name: win-chance numerator decoupled from the result numerator
guard: The guard that fires is Step 15. Step 15 (Win-Chance vs Result-Distribution Identity) requires the quoted win chance and the result distribution to be the same object.

name: theoretical RTP inflated above 1: a player-favourable price
guard: The guard that fires is Step 16. Step 16 (Effective-Edge Curve) must reject a player-favourable target.

name: simulation uniformity depth pin moved
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) binds the depth the artifact records to the constant in src/config.ts.

name: simulation serial-screen depth pin moved
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) recovers the serial depth from z = r1 x sqrt(n) at the artifact's own precision and compares it with the constant.

name: simulation effective-edge depth pin moved
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) requires every effective-edge sample in the artifact to carry n == SIM_EDGE_BETS.

name: simulation recorded seed changed in the artifact
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) binds the artifact's recorded master seed to SIM_MASTER_SEED and its bytes to the pin.

name: simulation recorded seed constant moved in src/config.ts
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) binds the artifact's recorded master seed to SIM_MASTER_SEED.

name: draw-bias bound: maxFair one past a whole number of ranges
find:
const maxFair = Math.floor(0x1_0000_0000 / range) * range;
  const wholeRanges
replace:
const maxFair = Math.floor(0x1_0000_0000 / range) * range + 1;
  const wholeRanges
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) asserts that maxFair is a whole number of ranges, so the per-value bias is exactly 0.

name: rejection guard removed from the draw: every 32-bit chunk accepted
guard: The guard that fires is Step 5. Step 5 (Draw & Result Recomputation) must reject a draw without the rejection guard (the same class as the guard-removed entry, by another edit): the first-chunk-rejected production rounds no longer recompute.

name: Pass-2 served-target rule loosened to fire below Z = 1
guard: The guard that fires is Step 24. Step 24 (Simulation Pass 2) must be able to fire: with the rule at Z < 1 the measured Z of the production capture trips it.

name: Pass-2 replay shifted one nonce (window 0 no longer the captured rounds)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 24. Step 24 (Simulation Pass 2) requires window 0 to reproduce every captured result.

name: Pass-2 early/late screen: an assumed rate p0 = 0.0475 in place of the computed one
guard: The guard that fires is Step 24. Step 24 (Simulation Pass 2) holds the committed pass2 block to the re-derivation, every leaf.

name: Pass-2 artifact: flag count doctored 0 -> 1
guard: The guard that fires is Step 24. Step 24 (Simulation Pass 2) re-derives the whole pass2 block from the dataset and requires the committed block to equal it; Step 19 also fails on the pin.

name: Pass-2 artifact: servedReturn.zCritical forged just beyond the reproduction bound
guard: The guard that fires is Step 24. Step 24 (Simulation Pass 2) compares the committed pass2 block with the re-derivation at the reproduction bound (1e-14 absolute + 1e-12 relative); Step 19 also fails on the pin.

name: Step 16 band threshold moved up by one band width: targets inside the band read as beyond it
guard: The guard that fires is Step 16. Step 16 (Effective-Edge Curve) must FLAG (origin operator) when a target of the audited range is beyond the RTP-CLAIM band: the verdict becomes a Conditional Pass.

name: draw-domain guard in the result formula made unreachable
guard: Killed by the unit suite (npx mocha), not by a scored step: tests/limbo/rngTests.ts 'draw domain is enforced' requires resultMultiplier to throw outside [0, RANGE). No settled round carries a draw outside the domain, so no scored step can see this edit.

name: effective edge reported as the claimed label instead of derived
guard: Killed by the unit suite (npx mocha), not by a scored step: tests/limbo/rngTests.ts requires the edge to be derived per target (above 1.00% where ci does not divide 9.9e9).

name: M-C3i one uncaptured target (1,234.57x) priced 2 pp below the claim, table + record regenerated
find: acc.add(() => `target=${(ci / 100).toFixed(2)}`, Math.floor(N / ci) * ci, D, name);
replace: acc.add(() => `target=${(ci / 100).toFixed(2)}`, Math.floor(N / ci) * ci - (ci === 123457 ? D / 50 : 0), D, name); // MUTATION
guard: The guard that fires is Step 16. Step 16 (LIMBO-19): one setting misses the published figure by more than the band and nothing else changes. Target 1,234.57x (no captured round used it) is priced 2 pp lower where the RTP table prices it, so it returns about 97 %. With the table re-written and re-pinned and the record re-emitted (regen), the run must end RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5, Step 16 OVERSTATED: no earlier check may turn it into exit 1 or 2. Without regen the committed table no longer matches (Step 16 FAIL, exit 1). Limbo has no paytable file: the price is the formula floor(9.9e9/ci)*ci, so the cell is lowered at the one place the table reads it.

name: M-C3ii published figure raised to 99.25 % in the claim source, table + record regenerated
guard: The guard that fires is Step 16. Step 16 (LIMBO-19): the published figure raised where the verifier reads it (src/rtp-settings.ts RTP_CLAIM, also read by Step 16's effective-edge floor in tests/steps/edge.ts). Step 16 first FLAGs on its own (origin operator) and is then re-scored by the rule; the run must end RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5, Step 16 OVERSTATED, not a Conditional Pass.

name: result-cap distinct-draw pin raised (3 -> 4 draws above the cap)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 25. Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) counts the distinct draws (seed, client seed, nonce) covered by the requests whose raw value is above the cap: 3 in the pinned records (two of the four requests are one draw sent at two targets) against 4 fails.
